messages:
Sam (AE): Quick heads-up — NovaHealth procurement wants a bank-guarantee (they called it a bank guarantee/standby letter) instead of our usual invoice path for the EU pilot. They also pushed for EU-only data processing and customer KMS. Can legal/finance advise on acceptability and routing? Also they want pilot start next Tues. @Priya (legal) @Li (finance)

Priya (legal): Bank guarantees are fine in principle but we need beneficiary and payable-terms clear. If this is a direct orderform (not marketplace), we can accept a standby LC that references the signed orderform and names Redwood Inference, Inc. as beneficiary. For DPA: require EU processing clause + SCCs or EU Addendum + customer-managed KMS option. Will draft redline.

Omar (solutions): For the EU-only requirement we should provision a tenant in eu-west-1 with dedicated pilot capacity. That will add ~$2.8k/mo to the pilot cost. KMS: we can support a customer-managed AWS KMS key for encryption at rest, but need an onboarding ticket and IAM role to access.

Li (finance): We can work with a standby letter of credit (sLC). Treasury needs the bank details and must review the LC terms. We'll require LC to cover the full pilot amount plus a $400 admin hold. Also prefer digital signature and bank's SWIFT confirmation rather than wet ink.

Sam (AE): Customer PO info they just sent:
```
PO#: NH-2026-980
Type: Pilot (90 days)
Amount: EUR 16,500
Payment: Standby LC — Bank: GlobalTrust Bank, SWIFT GTBCEUR2
Billing contact: ap@novahealth.com
```

Priya (legal): Thanks. I'll add the following to the orderform redline: 1) LC must expressly reference the orderform number and Redwood Inference, Inc.; 2) LC expiry >= 30 days after pilot end; 3) Payment triggers tied to invoice schedule; 4) Data Processing Location = EU; 5) SCCs or EU Addendum executed; 6) Subprocessor list + 30-day notice; 7) KMS terms + key rotation responsibilities. Also add termination right if LC is not received 10 days prior to start.

Omar (solutions): If we require LC to be in place 10 days before start we may need to push pilot start out by a week. Also onboarding for customer KMS takes ~3-5 business days.

Li (finance): Confirming: treasury will accept scanned LC + bank SWIFT confirmation as long as the LC is irrevocable and beneficiary language is correct. They prefer not to route through AWS marketplace. If the customer insists on marketplace, LC won't be acceptable because AWS handles payment.

Sam (AE): Customer insists they "must have bank guarantee to satisfy internal audit" and that marketplace invoices are not acceptable. They asked if we can do a hybrid: pilot via direct orderform with LC, then production via marketplace. Is that doable?

Priya (legal): Yes — we can include a conversion clause: "Pilot will convert to marketplace subscription upon mutual agreement; absent conversion pilot terminates at end of term." Also include liability cap and data-return clause on termination. I'll attach the redline in this thread.

DocuSignBot: DocuSign: Envelope sent to NovaHealth procurement (ap@novahealth.com) for countersignature.

Sam (AE): Next steps: Priya to upload MSA+DPA+orderform redline (ETA 6 hours); Li to confirm exact LC language treasury needs (ETA 4 hours); Omar to prepare EU slot estimate and KMS onboarding checklist (ETA EOD). I'll ask customer whether scanned LC + SWIFT confirm is acceptable and request bank contact.

Priya (legal): Also note: request customer provide a corporate certificate to verify signatory. If they want wet-ink on the LC itself that's between them and bank; bank usually issues originals. We'll accept scanned bank-issued LC documents plus bank confirmation.

Sam (AE): Great. Pushing to get pilot kickoff aligned. I'll update after the procurement call in 2 hours. :rocket:
